entries.script: { X.append(Coll(3)) }  // JVM: REJECTS, ArrayStoreException "can not copy int[] into long[]": concatArrays allocates by the LEFT's ClassTag (long[], from X's runtime items) and System.arraycopy refuses the int[] right side (CollectionUtil.scala:34-42)

entries.name: append-empty-left-accept#2
entries.script: { E.append(Coll(3)) }  // JVM: ACCEPTS: Coll[Int](3). An EMPTY left side short-circuits — CollOverArray.append returns the right side as it is, with its own item type, and never allocates (CollsOverArrays.scala:48-57). The one row of this family that survives a mismatch

entries.name: append-empty-right-errored#3
entries.script: { Coll(3).append(E) }  // JVM: REJECTS, ArrayStoreException "can not copy long[] into int[]" — an empty RIGHT side does NOT short-circuit. System.arraycopy checks element types before length, so a ZERO-LENGTH long[] still refuses to copy into an int[]. This is the asymmetry worth knowing: empty on the left saves the call, empty on the right does not

entries.name: append-reference-items-accept#4
entries.script: { If(false, Coll(Coll(1)), Coll(Coll(2L))).append(Coll(Coll(3))) }  // JVM: ACCEPTS, and the result is a Coll[Coll[LONG]] — the left's RUNTIME item type, not the node's declared Coll[Coll[Int]]. REFERENCE items allocate as Coll[] and a Coll[] copies into a Coll[] whatever its own element type, so nothing throws

entries.name: append-unrelated-classes-errored#5
entries.script: { If(false, Coll(SELF), Coll(groupGenerator)).append(Coll(SELF)) }  // JVM: REJECTS, ArrayStoreException "can not copy sigma.Box[] into sigma.GroupElement[]". Reference items accept only while the classes are compatible; UNRELATED classes throw, so #4's acceptance is about Coll[]-into-Coll[] and not about references in general

entries.name: append-pair-items-errored#6
entries.script: { If(false, Coll((1, 1)), Coll((1L, 1L))).append(Coll((2, 2))) }  // JVM: REJECTS, ArrayStoreException "can not copy int[] into long[]": a pair collection is a PairOfCols, so append unzips it (CollsOverArrays.scala:379-382) and the clash happens on the underlying PRIMITIVE arrays
